description:
Menu and toolbar construction in org.eclipse.e4.ui.workbench.renderers.swt and ContributionsAnalyzer (org.eclipse.e4.ui.workbench) does work that scales with the number of contributions and repeats per menu, toolbar or item.

title: Workbench layout (workbench.xmi) is reset whenever system locale changes
description:
Let's make sure issue is not already fixed in latest builds first.  
- [x] I verified I can reproduce this issue against [latest Integration Build of Eclipse SDK](https://download.eclipse.org/eclipse/downloads/)

## Steps to reproduce

From a fresh installation and clean workspace:

* In `eclipse.ini`, above `-vmargs`, add `-nl` and `en_US` on separate lines
* Start Eclipse and create/open a workspace

I tried

* Customizing the layout (moving/closing views, changing the perspective) and exiting Eclipse normally
* Changing `eclipse.ini` to `-nl` / `en_GB` and starting Eclipse again with the same workspace

I expected: the customized layout to be restored, at least between sibling locale changes like `en_US` and `en_GB`.
Preferably no locale change should reset the UI layout.

But got: the layout is reset to defaults. Switching back to `en_US` resets it again, so it happens every time the locale differs from the previous run.
Preferences (`.metadata/.plugins/org.eclipse.core.runtime/.settings/*.prefs`) are kept; only the layout state in `.metadata/.plugins/org.eclipse.e4.workbench/workbench.xmi` is lost.

## Here is some relevant log output
No logs were generated by the UI reset. My .log file isn't even created for the test integration build workspace i've used.

## Tested under this environment:
* OS & version: Windows 10/11
* Eclipse IDE/Platform version (as shown in *Help > About*): 2026-09, 2026-12 (I20261112-2300)
* Reproduced on both my personal and work PCs.

## Community

- [x] I understand reporting an issue to this OSS project does not mandate anyone to fix it. Other contributors may consider the issue, or not, at their own convenience. The most efficient way to get it fixed is that I fix it myself and contribute it back as a good quality patch to the project.

```

Build id: I20261025-2300
```

title: Support showing whitespace characters in code minings and ghost text
description:
Rendering whitespace characters in unified-diff code minings and their overlay currently requires substantial custom painting code in Eclipse Compare. In eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform#2998, @HannesWell suggested evaluating whether this could be simplified by supporting whitespace rendering generally for code minings/ghost text.

Please investigate a reusable option for code minings/ghost text to show whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, and line delimiters), respecting the editor's whitespace visibility preferences. Unified diff and other consumers could then enable this option instead of implementing their own whitespace rendering. The goal is to reduce duplicated painting logic and maintenance effort while preserving text layout and highlighting.

Original suggestion: https://github.com/eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform/pull/2998#issuecomment-6300866580

title: ViewerComparator sorts by decorated labels of DecoratingStyledCellLabelProvider, which violates the comparator contract
description:
`ViewerComparator.getLabel` unwraps a `DecoratingLabelProvider` and sorts by the undecorated label (Bug 364735). It does not unwrap a `DecoratingStyledCellLabelProvider`. That is the label provider of every `CommonViewer`, which sets a `NavigatorDecoratingLabelProvider` derived from it. For those viewers the comparator sorts by the decorated text.

The `DecorationScheduler` computes decorations in a background job. The job writes them into the result cache through `internalPutResult` while the UI thread may be sorting. The label of an element then changes between two comparisons of one `Arrays.sort`, and TimSort throws:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Comparison method violates its general contract!
    at java.base/java.util.TimSort.mergeHi(TimSort.java:903)
    at java.base/java.util.TimSort.mergeAt(TimSort.java:520)
    at java.base/java.util.TimSort.mergeForceCollapse(TimSort.java:461)
    at java.base/java.util.TimSort.sort(TimSort.java:254)
    at java.base/java.util.Arrays.sort(Arrays.java:1234)
    at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.TreePathViewerSorter.sort(TreePathViewerSorter.java:105)
    at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.AbstractTreeViewer.getSortedChildren(AbstractTreeViewer.java:685)
    at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.AbstractTreeViewer.updateChildren(AbstractTreeViewer.java:2907)
    at org.eclipse.jface.viewers.AbstractTreeViewer.internalRefreshStruct(AbstractTreeViewer.java:2032)
    ...
    at org.eclipse.ui.navigator.CommonViewer.refresh(CommonViewer.java:370)
```

A trace in the sorter of our product caught the label change in a Common Navigator with 120 Git-shared projects during a build:

```
label of P/plcSample105 changed during one sort from 'plcSample105' to '> plcSample105 [plcSample105 master]'
```

A second effect: the EGit dirty prefix `> ` sorts before letters, so dirty projects move to the top of a group once their decoration is cached.

**To Reproduce**

1. Common Navigator with at least 32 elements under one parent, all shared with EGit so that their labels carry text decorations. TimSort checks the contract from 32 elements upward.
2. Change the Git state of many elements at once, for example by touching a file in each project. The decorations are then recomputed while the viewer refreshes.
3. The failure depends on timing. It needs a decoration result to arrive during one sort, so it does not happen on every refresh.

**Expected behavior**

`ViewerComparator` sorts by the undecorated label for the styled decorating providers as it does for `DecoratingLabelProvider`.

**Proposed fix**

In `ViewerComparator.getLabel`, read the undecorated text of a `DelegatingStyledCellLabelProvider` through its styled string provider:

```java
if (prov instanceof DelegatingStyledCellLabelProvider delegating) {
	StyledString text = delegating.getStyledStringProvider().getStyledText(e1);
	name1 = text == null ? null : text.getString();
} else if (prov instanceof ILabelProvider lprov) {
	if (lprov instanceof DecoratingLabelProvider dprov) {
		lprov = dprov.getLabelProvider();
	}
	name1 = lprov.getText(e1);
} else {
	name1 = e1.toString();
}
```

**Environment**

- Eclipse Platform 4.38 (org.eclipse.jface 3.38.100, org.eclipse.ui.navigator 3.13.300). `ViewerComparator.getLabel` in master has the same code.
- Java 21, Windows 11.

title: Re-enabling theming requires two restarts instead of one
description:
<!-- Thank you for reporting this issue! -->
<!-- The following template is highly recommended to trigger an efficient course of actions: it's pretty suitable if you're not familiar with the project as it will guide you in sharing the most important information. If you're not comfortable with this template for your particular report, feel free to erase it and write your report from scratch -->

After disabling theming and restarting, if the user re-checks Enable Theming and clicks Apply, Eclipse restarts. After that restart theming is active but no theme has been selected or applied. The user must open Preferences a second time, pick a theme, and restart again. Two restarts are required to get back to a themed state.

## Steps to reproduce

From a fresh installation and clean workspace:

1. Open Window → Preferences → General → Appearance with theming enabled.
2. Uncheck Enable Theming, click Apply, and restart when prompted.
3. After restart, open Window → Preferences → General → Appearance.
4. Re-check Enable Theming, click Apply, and restart when prompted.
5. Current Beha: Eclipse starts with theming on but no theme applied — the workbench has no CSS styling. User must open Preferences again, select a theme, and restart a third time.
6. Expected: After step 4's restart, Eclipse starts with theming on and a theme already applied — one restart total.

title: Move generic breadcrumb implementation from JDT to JFace
description:
The breadcrumb implementation currently used by the JDT Java editor contains
generic viewer infrastructure that is not specific to Java.

Move the reusable breadcrumb viewer implementation to
org.eclipse.jface.viewers and adapt JDT to use the JFace implementation.

The refactoring keeps JDT-specific behavior in JDT through extension hooks,
including:
- ProblemTreeViewer for the drop-down viewer
- Java-specific element openability semantics
- persistent dialog settings

The goal is to make the breadcrumb viewer reusable by other clients while
preserving the existing Java editor behavior.

The change spans eclipse.platform.ui and eclipse.jdt.ui and will be submitted
as coordinated pull requests.

title: Provide more options to configure the NotificationPopup
description:
<!-- Thanks for suggesting an enhancement! -->
<!-- The following template is highly recommended to trigger an efficient course of actions: it's pretty suitable if you're not familiar with the project as it will guide you in sharing the most important information. If you're not comfortable with this template for your particular report, feel free to erase it and write your report from scratch -->

Let's make sure issue is not already fixed in latest builds first.

- [x] I verified [latest Integration Build of Eclipse SDK](https://download.eclipse.org/eclipse/downloads/) doesn't provide the feature.

## Suggestion

The NotificationPopup (org.eclipse.jface.notifications) has some minor flaws, where some workarounds are necessary.

* The MIN_HEIGHT, MAX_WIDTH and PADDING_EDGE of the popup cannot be configured as desired, as it is hardcoded in the AbstractNotificationPopup.

To shrink the height of the popup, I needed to create a workaround like this:
```java
Point size = popup.getShell().getSize();
Point location = popup.getShell().getLocation();
popup.getShell().pack();
popup.getShell().setLocation(location.x, location.y + (size.y - popup.getShell().getSize().y));
```
It would be nice to have these options in the builder like this:

```java
NotificationPopup.forDisplay(Display.getDefault())
    .text("A problem occurred.")
    .title("Warning", true)
    .minHeight(0)
    .maxWidth(500)
    .paddingEdge(10)
    .open();
```

* The Popup does not follow its parent shell, when it is moved or resized. It would be nice to have an option for this when creating the popup (or maybe as default behavior)

The listener could look like this:
```java
    static void attachPopupFollower(Shell parentShell, Shell popupShell, int padding) {
        Listener moveListener = e -> {
            if (parentShell == null || parentShell.isDisposed()) {
                return;
            }
            if (popupShell == null || popupShell.isDisposed()) {
                return;
            }

            Rectangle clientArea = parentShell.getClientArea();
            Point clientOriginOnDisplay = parentShell.toDisplay(clientArea.x, clientArea.y);
            Point popupSize = popupShell.getSize();

            int x = clientOriginOnDisplay.x + clientArea.width - popupSize.x - padding; //use the configured paddingEdge here
            int y = clientOriginOnDisplay.y + clientArea.height - popupSize.y - padding;

            popupShell.setLocation(x, y);
        };

        parentShell.addListener(SWT.Move, moveListener);
        parentShell.addListener(SWT.Resize, moveListener);

        popupShell.addListener(SWT.Dispose, e -> {
            if (!parentShell.isDisposed()) {
                parentShell.removeListener(SWT.Move, moveListener);
                parentShell.removeListener(SWT.Resize, moveListener);
            }
        });
    }
```

I attached the whole example as a file here.

## Community

- [x] I understand suggesting an enhancement doesn't mandate anyone to implement it. Other contributors may consider this suggestion, or not, at their own convenience. The most efficient way to get it fixed is that I implement it myself and contribute it back as a good quality patch to the project.

title: Use the shared color blend helper from SWT
description:
Blending two `RGB` values by a ratio is implemented over a dozen times in platform.ui, each with its own parameter type and rounding.
Following the discussion in #4489, SWT now provides the shared helper: `RGB.blend(RGB other, double weight)` and `RGBA.blend(RGBA other, double weight)` (eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform.swt#3732, `@since 3.136`).
The weight is the share of `other`, from 0 (the receiver) to 1 (`other`), and channels are rounded to the nearest integer.

Work to do in platform.ui, once SWT 3.136 is in the target platform:

- Raise the `org.eclipse.swt` lower bound to 3.136 in each touched bundle's `MANIFEST.MF`.
- Replace the private copies with `RGB.blend`:

| Bundle | Copy | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| jface | `PopupDialog.blend(bg, fg, factor)` | `bg.blend(fg, factor)` |
| jface.databinding | `SWTUtil.mix(rgb1, rgb2, ratio)` | `rgb2.blend(rgb1, ratio)` |
| jface.text | `Colors.blend(bg, fg, factor)`, projection `SourceViewerInformationControl.blend` | `bg.blend(fg, factor)` |
| jface.text | `OverviewRuler.interpolate(fg, bg, scale)`, `DiffPainter.interpolate` | `fg.blend(bg, scale)` |
| ui.editors | `SourceViewerInformationControl.blend(bg, fg, factor)` | `bg.blend(fg, factor)` |
| ui.workbench | `ShowViewDialog.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` | `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)` |
| ui.workbench | `HeapStatus.blend(fg, bg)` (40% foreground) | `bg.getRGB().blend(fg.getRGB(), 0.4)` |
| e4 renderers | `CTabRendering.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` | `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)` |

- Keep the public API and let it delegate: `FormColors.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` and `ColorUtil.blend(c1, c2, ratio)` become `c2.blend(c1, ratio / 100.0)`, and `ColorUtil.blend(val1, val2)` becomes `val1.blend(val2, 0.5)`.

The copies truncate while `RGB.blend` rounds, so a migrated color can differ by one per channel.
Tests that compare exact RGB values need adjusting rather than a rounding shim.

Copies in other repositories (Compare in eclipse.platform, JDT UI, PDE, GEF Classic's `FigureUtilities`) can follow the same way.
